1.note: literally, “gird up the waist of your mind” or “put on the belt of the waist of your mind”

2.note: “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה” or “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
“Overseer” is from the Greek ἐπίσκοπον, which can mean overseer, curator, guardian, or superintendent.
